'''Nora Isobel Calderwood''' (14 March 1896 – April 1985) was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[professor]] and [[mathematician]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=The use of single-core sheathed cables for alternating currents|last=Cramp|first=W.|last2=Calderwood|first2=Nora I.|journal=Journal of the Institution of Electrical Engineers|year=1923|volume=61 |issue=317|pages=477–485|doi=10.1049/jiee-1.1923.0067}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cramp|first=W.|last2=Calderwood|first2=Nora I.|journal=Journal of the Institution of Electrical Engineers|year=1923|volume=61 |issue=323|pages=1061–1071|doi=10.1049/jiee-1.1923.0136|title= The calculation of air-space flux}}</ref>

== Early life and education==
Calderwood was born in 1896 in [[Blairgowrie and Rattray|Blairgowrie]], [[Perthshire]], in Scotland. Her father Daniel Scott Calderwood was the headmaster of the Blairgowrie Public School. Her family then moved to [[Edinburgh]] when she was still young, after her father was appointed as the headmaster of the Church of Scotland Normal School.<ref name=":0">{{MacTutor|id=Calderwood|title=Nora Isobel Calderwood}}</ref>

Calderwood started at James Gillespie's School in 1901, at the age of five, staying for six years. On receiving a bursary from the Edinburgh Burgh Committee on Secondary Education, she studied at Edinburgh Ladies' College from 1907 to 1914.<ref name=":0" /> In 1910, at the age of 14, she passed Higher Piano, and in 1913 was named the dux of the music classes at Edinburgh Ladies' College. She was also awarded the prize to the best Science scholar and best Arithmetician, both of which she resigned, and the Costorphine Prize for the best mathematician.<ref name=":0" />

Calderwood studied at the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 1914 to 1920, earning a [[Bachelor of Science]] (Pure) in 1919 and a [[Master of Arts]] in Political Economy in 1920. Courses taken include mathematics, Latin, natural philosophy and chemistry.<ref name=":0" /> She joined the faculty of the [[University of Birmingham]] the following year, lecturing in mathematics. Soon, however, she returned to Edinburgh to continue her studies under mathematician [[Alexander Aitken]], earning a [[PhD]] in mathematics from the university in 1931 with a thesis on ''Researches in the Theory of Matrices.''<ref name=phd>{{Cite thesis|title=Researches in the theory of matrices|last=Calderwood|first=Nora I.|publisher=University of Edinburgh|year=1931|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.642319}}}}</ref>
<ref name=":0" /><ref name=mathgene/><ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Calderwood|first=N. R.|date=1931|title=Researches in the theory of matrices|hdl=1842/29038|language=en|publisher=University of Edinburgh}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Calderwood was a member of [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]] joined in 1919 as an undergraduate, and the [[London Mathematical Society]], joined in 1922.<ref name=":0" />

She is fondly listed by a student, Margaret Lee née Ireland (1962 BSc Mathematics) as one of her favourite memories: "Dr Nora Calderwood - what a woman who loved us so much, she could barely keep exam questions secret".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.birmingham.ac.uk/Documents/alumni/Memories/MemoriesandMessagesfromtheClassof1962.pdf|title=Memories and Messages from the Class of 1962|year=2016|publisher=The University of Birmingham|website=birmingham.ac.uk|author=Anon|access-date=2016-10-11}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Hers is the [[namesake]] for the Calderwood Prize, an academic award at the [[University of Birmingham]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.birmingham.ac.uk/schools/mathematics/undergraduate/grants-scholarships.aspx|title=Scholarships and prizes, Undergraduates, School of Mathematics - University of Birmingham|website=birmingham.ac.uk|access-date=2016-05-11|author=Anon|year=2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160512054426/http://www.birmingham.ac.uk/schools/mathematics/undergraduate/grants-scholarships.aspx|archive-date=12 May 2016|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Calderwood never married.<ref name=":0" /> She was an accomplished piano player, and gave recitals at [[Birmingham]].<ref name=":0" />
